items.title: Earl Humphrey Interview, 1963-03-28
items.q: I introduced him to Ma Rainey and George Washington and the whole cast sitting up there waiting for a telegram.

ctx.x: I said, man. I said, man. I said, man. I can't get any out of this fella's thick. I said, man. I can't get any out of this fella's thick. I said, you ain't doing nothing out of here, man. You're sleeping in the station here waiting for Ma Rainey to... get some tickets from Baton Rouge or somewhere to pull you all in there. And then two chairs in one. She's gonna take all the money. She's gonna take all the money. Still ain't gonna have nothing.

And I, the man was in the place, Cameron. I called him on the side, I said, man, I get about $75. What you gonna do with the money? I said, well, one of my good friends right there stranded. I'm gonna send him home. Who is that friend? When he come over the station, he didn't know George Washington. Little bit of fella played trombone. Good trombone player. I introduced him to Ma Rainey and George Washington and the whole cast sitting up there waiting for a telegram. Come from Baton Rouge somewhere to pull him…
